notes:
I couldn't write any notes this time, because my research tools stopped working before I could read a single source.

My first search ("enduringword John 1 commentary") returned data in a format my script didn't expect, and the script crashed. When I tried again, the tool told me I had used up my searches for this turn. So I didn't get to open any commentary pages: not Enduring Word, Bible Hub, Preceptaustin, NET Bible notes or anything else on your list.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. Writing notes from memory would break all three, so I've left the notes empty rather than make anything up.

**If you start a new turn, this is what I'll look up:**

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - Enduring Word on John 1
   - Bible Hub commentaries on each verse (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary)
   - Preceptaustin's John 1 page
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
   - v. 9, "light to every man": Wesleyan teaching on grace that comes before faith (wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed.com) against Reformed sources (ligonier.org, monergism.com)
   - vv. 12–13, whether new birth comes before faith: Reformed and Baptist sources (desiringgod.org, gty.org) against Wesleyan ones
   - vv. 12–13, new birth and baptism: Lutheran sources (lcms.org, 1517.org)
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes on v. 1 ("the Word was God"), v. 5 ("overcome" or "understood") and v. 18 (whether the oldest manuscripts say "only Son" or "only God")
   - Bible Odyssey on John's idea of "the Word"
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings: Chrysostom's sermons on John (newadvent.org), catholic.com on v. 1, and oca.org on John 1 as the Easter gospel reading
   - Hyper-grace teaching on v. 17 (law through Moses, grace through Jesus), as described on gotquestions.org and similar sites

Shall I try again in a new turn? I can do the whole passage at once, or take a few verses at a time so I can read each source properly.
